Subject: Re: Increased first-token latency (TTFT) since 08:30 PT — initial triage

Triage notes (brief):
- Correlated trace id rdx:acme:trace:20260302:7751 to egress logs. Backend inference execution times are within normal bounds (median token gen ~12ms).
- The anomaly is in "first-byte"/first-token timing (TTFT): we see p95 ~780ms (baseline ~190ms) and p99 ~1820ms (baseline ~420ms) for edge -> origin path between ~08:30–09:10 PT.
- Packet-level logs show elevated TLS handshake times (full handshake RTT) to a single CDN POP in us-west-2 region; increased TCP SYN->ACK RTT and repeated full handshakes (session resumption not being honored).
- Error rate (502/504) also ticked up from 0.18% to 1.6% during window — likely client timeouts while handshake in progress.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: degradation at the upstream CDN/edge POP (TLS handshake latencies and connection churn), causing increased TTFT despite backend being healthy. Could be a transient control-plane issue at the CDN or a routing flapping event.

Immediate mitigations we can take (recommended order):
1) Enable TLS session resumption (tickets) and increase session validity for outbound edge connections to reduce full-handshake frequency.
2) Increase keepalive / connection idle timeout for affected POPs to reduce new-handshake rate.
3) Temporarily steer Acme traffic away from the affected POP to an alternate POP/region (requires permission and will briefly route via different latency profile).
4) As a short-term defensive measure, extend client timeout thresholds for the next 30–60 minutes (if Acme agrees) to avoid failed workflows.

I can implement 1+2 within ~15 minutes; steering (3) needs a 10–20 minute rollout plus validation. We should notify the customer before steering.

I'll proceed to enable session resumption and bump keepalive unless you tell me not to. Also attaching a short set of graphs (p95/p99 before/after) once I have them.

—Dev Patel
SRE — Inference Serving

Subject: Re: Increased first-token latency (TTFT) since 08:30 PT — proposed immediate fixes

Oliver — quick update and proposed immediate steps from engineering:

Summary: our backend is healthy; the spike is isolated to TLS handshake/edge POP behavior. Engineering proposes to:
- Enable TLS session resumption + slightly longer session validity (reduces full handshakes).
- Increase connection keepalive so active connections persist longer.
- If that isn't sufficient we will steer your traffic away from the affected POP.

Impact: both changes are low-risk and reversible; we expect p95 TTFT to drop substantially if the issue is handshake-related.

Can we get permission to apply the session-resumption + keepalive changes immediately? If you prefer, we can roll to 50% of your traffic first and monitor.

If you approve, we will perform changes in the next 15 minutes and update within 30.

—Sean

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:28:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased first-token latency (TTFT) since 08:30 PT — mitigation applied and metrics

Action taken: enabled TLS session resumption + extended session validity; increased keepalive on edge connections for Acme route; rolled change to 50% traffic at 10:10 PT, then to 100% after 10:22 PT once metrics validated.

Results (measured at 10:30 PT):
- p50 TTFT: 48ms (baseline ~45ms)
- p95 TTFT: 220ms (pre-mitigation ~780ms)
- p99 TTFT: 420ms (pre-mitigation ~1820ms)
- Error rate: dropped from 1.6% -> 0.21% (back near baseline)

Attached: grafana_p95_p99_before_after.png, logs_p95_spike_20260302.zip (trimmed). Links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/TTFT/acme-p95-overview (live panel).

Root cause (update): strong correlation with a single CDN POP in us-west-2 failing to resume TLS sessions reliably. We believe it to be a transient issue in the CDN edge control plane. We're opening a support ticket with the CDN provider and requesting a postmortem.

Follow-ups:
- Recommend we implement persistent connection pre-warming and session ticket pinning for top-traffic accounts (Acme included) as a medium-term fix.
- Recommend a small credit to Acme for the incident window (Monica can handle).
- Engineering will add a detection alert for sudden TLS handshake RTT skew by POP so we can auto-failover faster.

I'll leave monitoring on for the next 24 hours and post any regression.

—Dev

Subject: ACME — incident summary and ask for exec decision on credit

Markus / Evelyn —

Summary of today's incident with Acme Logistics:
- Symptom: sustained TTFT p95/p99 regressions and elevated error rates between ~08:30–09:10 PT. Customer reported impact to onboarding flows.
- Cause: transient failure at an upstream CDN POP causing increased TLS handshake latency and repeated full-handshakes (session resumption not honored). Backend inference latency remained normal.
- Mitigation: engineering enabled TLS session resumption and increased keepalive; traffic was ramped to alternate POPs for validation. Post-mitigation p95 dropped from ~780ms -> 220ms; p99 from ~1820ms -> 420ms; error rate returned near baseline.
- Current status: resolved; monitoring in place; CDN ticket opened for postmortem.

Action requested: Monica recommends a goodwill credit for Acme for the ~40 minute window of degraded performance. Proposed credit: one month of our Dedicated base fee prorated (equivalent to $14,000). Monica can provide exact figures.

Please advise if we should proceed with the proposed credit and any additional outreach (exec call with Acme leadership).

Thanks — will keep you posted on CDN postmortem.

—Sean
